Answer

This page is the docs hub for the FAIRagro Advanced Middleware family: API, Harvester, and SQL-to-ARC.

  1. Middleware API: harvest ingest writes CouchDB immediately and publishes asynchronously via Celery.12
  2. Harvester: catalog plugins discover, parse, and map into HarvestedArc, then upload RO-Crate JSON.
  3. SQL-to-ARC: ISA-shaped SQL views carry the domain mapping; the converter assembles and uploads.
  4. Standalone Archify viewers for every diagram are linked from the catalog below.

How does the Middleware API fit together?

Diagram structure

  • SearchHUB searchhub

  • api → couchdb · writes ARCs
  • api → rabbitmq · enqueue
  • worker → rabbitmq · consumes
  • worker → couchdb · writes events
  • worker → arc-store · sync_arc
  • worker → consol-store · finalize

Full page: System overview

  1. RDI client ↗

    Delivers RO-Crate to the API over mTLS.

  2. Middleware API ↗

    AuthZ and sync store; enqueues tasks.

  3. CouchDB ↗

    Durable ARC and harvest documents.

  4. RabbitMQ ↗

    Celery broker between API enqueue and the worker.

  5. Celery worker ↗

    Calls the store ports.

  6. Store ports ↗

    ArcStore and ConsolidatedArcStore are two ports on the worker, wired side by side: per-ARC publish vs catalog. At runtime, finalize runs after ARC sync.34

  7. Datahub ↗

    Git hosting for ARC repos and the catalog.

  8. SearchHUB ↗

    External consumer context; not wired here.

Full page: API process internals

  1. RDI client ↗

    Calls the API over mTLS with RO-Crate ARCs.

  2. FastAPI / Routes ↗

    Accepts harvest/ARC requests.5

  3. BusinessLogic ↗

    mode=api: stores ARC/metadata, enqueues sync.6

  4. DocumentStore ↗

    Reads existing doc; writes ARC + last_seen ….7

  5. TaskDispatcher ↗

    Enqueue to RabbitMQ.2

  6. RabbitMQ ↗

    Broker sink of the API process: sync tasks leave here.

What is inside the Celery worker process?

Diagram structure

  • BL-Manager bl-mgr
  • Celery Tasks tasks

  • consol → datahub · writes catalog

Full page: Worker process internals

  1. RabbitMQ ↗

    Source of worker work: delivers sync and finalize tasks.

  2. Celery tasks ↗

    Entry: sync_arc_to_gitlab with full ARC JSON-LD, finalize_catalog with RDI.8

  3. BusinessLogic ↗

    Drives sync and finalize; does not read ARCs from CouchDB itself.2

  4. DocumentStore ↗

    Sync: BL writes events only; finalize: ConsolidatedArcStore reads ARC content.910

  5. Store ports ↗

    ArcStore writes each ARC repo; ConsolidatedArcStore reads ARCs from CouchDB and writes the catalog. Parallel ports; finalize follows sync.310

  6. Datahub ↗

    Sink: ARC repos and catalog land in Git hosting.

6

How does the Harvester produce ARCs?

Full pages: Harvester overview · Discover / Parse / Map

  • Plugins (INSPIRE, generic Protocol, OAI-PMH) discover catalog records and map them to HarvestedArc.
  • Shared PayloadParser / DataMapper registries sit in the middle; INSPIRE bypasses the shared parser.
  • The orchestrator unwraps HarvestedArc.arc_json (RO-Crate JSON) and uploads via ApiClient.harvest_arcs.
7

How does SQL-to-ARC produce ARCs?

Full pages: SQL-to-ARC overview · SQL → ARC data flow

  • Domain mapping to ISA/ARC shape lives in the RDI SQL views, not in the converter code.
  • The converter validates and streams those views, mechanically assembles ARCtrl objects, and uploads RO-Crate JSON.
  • Same Middleware API sink as the Harvester (harvest_arcs under mTLS).
